This is Lay-by Smart, live on Avalanche Fuji. One customer, three lay-bys, each with its own agreement ID, read straight from the smart contract.
She pays an instalment on the TV. The payment screen names the exact lay-by and the shop. Every instalment names its lay-by.
Here is the receipt, with a public record on Snowtrace. Only the TV balance moved.
Now a stranger tries to pay into her lay-by. The contract refuses: only the customer can pay. Nothing was signed, and no gas was spent.
She tries to overpay, and is refused again. Then she pays the full balance, and the lay-by is completed. The money waits in the contract, not the till.
Once she has the TV in hand, she confirms collection. Only then is the money released to the shop.
She cancels the fridge. The fee and her refund are shown before she signs. The fee was fixed up front, never more than one percent.
The sofa ran past its date. The shop settles the expiry, and the rule splits the money. Nobody negotiates.
Every step is a public record on Avalanche. Lay-by Smart: fair lay-by, on chain.
